claims.text: The program introduces its private school rules as one list of things a school must meet.
claims.quote: To participate in the program, private schools must meet the following eligibility requirements:
claims.verbatim_quote: To participate in the program, private schools must meet the following eligibility requirements:

claims.text: The first published requirement is accreditation.
claims.quote: Be accredited by an organization recognized by the Texas Private School Accreditation Commission (TEPSAC) or by the Texas Education Agency.
claims.verbatim_quote: Be accredited by an organization recognized by the Texas Private School Accreditation Commission (TEPSAC) or by the Texas Education Agency.

claims.text: The second is a record of having run a campus.
claims.quote: Be a proven operator that has successfully run a campus for at least two years.
claims.verbatim_quote: Be a proven operator that has successfully run a campus for at least two years.

claims.text: The third is a test.
claims.quote: Administer a nationally norm-referenced assessment.
claims.verbatim_quote: Administer a nationally norm-referenced assessment.

claims.text: The fourth is a location.
claims.quote: Be located in Texas or, for a virtual school, have an office in Texas.
claims.verbatim_quote: Be located in Texas or, for a virtual school, have an office in Texas.

claims.text: The program takes school applications continuously rather than in a window.
claims.quote: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
claims.verbatim_quote: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

claims.text: The private school application period has a published opening date.
claims.quote: The application period for private schools opened on December 9, 2025.
claims.verbatim_quote: The application period for private schools opened on December 9, 2025.

claims.text: The state has set what follows a child to an approved private school next year.
claims.quote: The Texas Education Agency (TEA) has determined the amount for the 2026-27 school year is $10,474 per child if the student attends an approved private school.
claims.verbatim_quote: The Texas Education Agency (TEA) has determined the amount for the 2026-27 school year is $10,474 per child if the student attends an approved private school.

claims.text: Alpha School says on its own front page what delivers the coursework.
claims.quote: Our AI tutor gives students 1:1 personalized education, providing coursework at their individual pace and the appropriate level.
claims.verbatim_quote: Our AI tutor gives students 1:1 personalized education, providing coursework at their individual pace and the appropriate level.

claims.text: The same page says what the adults in the room do instead of teaching.
claims.quote: Adults, whether teachers or parents, become 'Guides,' shifting the traditional teacher-student relationship to offer motivational and emotional support.
claims.verbatim_quote: Adults, whether teachers or parents, become 'Guides,' shifting the traditional teacher-student relationship to offer motivational and emotional support.

claims.text: The same page carries a performance claim.
claims.quote: Alpha classes learn twice as fast as their peers and rank in the top 1% nationwide.
claims.verbatim_quote: Alpha classes learn twice as fast as their peers and rank in the top 1% nationwide.

claims.text: The school names the technology that carries the core subjects.
claims.quote: Our 2hr Learning model harnesses adaptive technology to provide students 1:1 learning, accelerating mastery over core subjects.
claims.verbatim_quote: Our 2hr Learning model harnesses adaptive technology to provide students 1:1 learning, accelerating mastery over core subjects.

claims.text: The school says the academic part of the day ends before the afternoon.
claims.quote: With academics completed in the mornings, they get their afternoons back to gain real-world skills and explore interests, all at school.
claims.verbatim_quote: With academics completed in the mornings, they get their afternoons back to gain real-world skills and explore interests, all at school.

claims.text: On the charter route the education commissioner is the one who recommends.
claims.quote: Under state law, the Commissioner of Education is responsible for recommending new open-enrollment charters to the SBOE.
claims.verbatim_quote: Under state law, the Commissioner of Education is responsible for recommending new open-enrollment charters to the SBOE.

claims.text: On that route an elected board can refuse, and it has.
claims.quote: The SBOE vetoed the granting of a charter to Unidos Soccer Leadership Academy (San Antonio) and Valenta Academy (Bastrop).
claims.verbatim_quote: The SBOE vetoed the granting of a charter to Unidos Soccer Leadership Academy (San Antonio) and Valenta Academy (Bastrop).

claims.text: The charter cycle carries its own line on the board's published agenda.
claims.quote: Open-Enrollment Charter School Generation 32 Application Updates
claims.verbatim_quote: Open-Enrollment Charter School Generation 32 Application Updates
claims.source_title: Texas State Board of Education, agenda, August 31 to September 4, 2026

claims.text: The agenda says what that line is for.
claims.quote: This item provides an opportunity for the committee to receive updates regarding the Generation 32 Open-Enrollment Charter Application cycle.
claims.verbatim_quote: This item provides an opportunity for the committee to receive updates regarding the Generation 32 Open-Enrollment Charter Application cycle.
claims.source_title: Texas State Board of Education, agenda, August 31 to September 4, 2026

claims.text: The agenda records what the board did with it.
claims.quote: SBOE - NO ACTION
claims.verbatim_quote: SBOE - NO ACTION
claims.source_title: Texas State Board of Education, agenda, August 31 to September 4, 2026

claims.text: The board's own agenda dates the meeting.
claims.quote: State Board of Education, August 31-September 4, 2026
claims.verbatim_quote: State Board of Education, August 31-September 4, 2026
claims.source_title: Texas State Board of Education, agenda, August 31 to September 4, 2026

claims.text: A spokesperson for the voucher program said the charter rejection did not bear on it.
claims.quote: "That wasn't relevant," said Travis Pillow, a spokesperson for the voucher program.
claims.verbatim_quote: "That wasn't relevant," said Travis Pillow, a spokesperson for the voucher program.
claims.source_title: ProPublica and The Texas Tribune, September 2nd, 2026

claims.text: The same spokesperson described what the program checks.
claims.quote: "Our role is to make sure that a school meets the requirements in the law."
claims.verbatim_quote: "Our role is to make sure that a school meets the requirements in the law."
claims.source_title: ProPublica and The Texas Tribune, September 2nd, 2026

claims.text: Reporting found how far the school has grown in Texas and how it fared in the program.
claims.quote: Now, just one year after the state rejected its charter school application, Alpha has roughly quadrupled its Texas private schools, with more than 30 virtual and in-person campuses, most of which were accepted into the voucher program, ProPublica and The Texas Tribune found.
claims.verbatim_quote: Now, just one year after the state rejected its charter school application, Alpha has roughly quadrupled its Texas private schools, with more than 30 virtual and in-person campuses, most of which were accepted into the voucher program, ProPublica and The Texas Tribune found.
claims.source_title: ProPublica and The Texas Tribune, September 2nd, 2026

claims.text: Reporting states the board turned the school down.
claims.quote: Even the largely conservative Texas State Board of Education, which had approved most charter applications over the last decade, rejected Alpha's pitch last summer.
claims.verbatim_quote: Even the largely conservative Texas State Board of Education, which had approved most charter applications over the last decade, rejected Alpha's pitch last summer.
claims.source_title: ProPublica and The Texas Tribune, September 2nd, 2026

claims.text: Reporting states what the board's stated worries counted for afterward.
claims.quote: None of the concerns raised by the Texas board just last year about Alpha's rejected charter applications, test scores or use of AI to teach mattered.
claims.verbatim_quote: None of the concerns raised by the Texas board just last year about Alpha's rejected charter applications, test scores or use of AI to teach mattered.
claims.source_title: ProPublica and The Texas Tribune, September 2nd, 2026

absences.looked_for: any sentence on the page referring to curriculum, instructional method, teaching method, teachers, or software
absences.method: A complete sentence inventory of the page was taken rather than a keyword search, 8 headings and 29 body sentences, so the finding is measured against everything the page says.
absences.found: None. The sentences cover accreditation, operating history, a norm-referenced assessment, a Texas location, separate pre-K and kindergarten provider criteria, the application window, the transfer amount, out of state use, a copyright line and a cookie notice.
absences.slide_safe_statement: The four published requirements are accreditation, two years of operation, a nationally norm-referenced assessment, and a Texas location. None of the four concerns curriculum, instructional method, or who or what does the teaching.

absences.found: Nothing. The nearest text is more of the same copy. No footnote, asterisk, study name or test name appears anywhere on the page.
absences.slide_safe_statement: The front page offers no source, no study and no test for either figure.
